llm.reply:
Marfan syndrome is a heritable connective tissue disorder whose phenotype spans multiple organ systems [22: "a multisystem connective tissue disease with autosomal dominant inheritance"]. It is mainly attributed to FBN1 mutations, and its presentation varies between patients [22: "It is mainly caused by FBN1 gene mutation and often has different clinical manifestations"].

## Catalogued Clinical Features

MedGen lists these clinical features: Aortic regurgitation [7], Arachnodactyly [11], Astigmatism [15], Ectopia lentis [19], Esotropia [23], Exotropia [25], Pes planus [26], Glaucoma [27], Congestive heart failure [28], Hypertropia [29] and Micrognathia [30]. The MedGen concept for this condition is titled Marfan syndrome [2].

## Diagnosis and Severity

The revised Ghent nosology is central to making the diagnosis [24: "The Ghent II Nosology of MFS criteria are crucial in MFS diagnosis"]. The neonatal form is uncommon and carries a worse outlook [22: "Neonatal MFS is especially rare with severe conditions and a poor prognosis"]. No curative therapy exists yet, but early detection and treatment can extend survival [22: "there is still no radical treatment method for MFS, but early identification, early diagnosis, and early treatment can effectively prolong the life span of patients"].

## Aortic Therapeutic Trials

The cardiovascular phenotype has been a focus of clinical trials, including Comparison of Two Medications Aimed at Slowing Aortic Root Enlargement in Individuals With Marfan Syndrome [8]. Another trial is Losartan Versus Atenolol for the Treatment of Marfan Syndrome [16]. A further trial is Angiotensin Converting Enzyme Inhibitors in Marfan Syndrome [12].

MedGen lists these clinical features: Aortic regurgitation [7], Arachnodactyly [11], Astigmatism [15], Ectopia lentis [19], Esotropia [23], Exotropia [25], Pes planus [26], Glaucoma [27], Congestive heart failure [28], Hypertropia [29] and Micrognathia [30]. Marfan syndrome is a heritable connective tissue disorder that affects many body systems [22: "Marfan syndrome (MFS) is a multisystem connective tissue disease with autosomal dominant inheritance"]. Its features vary between patients [22: "It is mainly caused by FBN1 gene mutation and often has different clinical manifestations"].

## Disease records

The MedGen concept is titled Marfan syndrome [2]. The literature entity is named Marfan Syndrome [3]. One PubMed record is titled Marfan syndrome. [1] Another PubMed record is titled Marfan syndrome. [14] A third PubMed record is titled Marfan syndrome. [18]

## Clinical course and diagnosis

The neonatal form is rare and severe [22: "Neonatal MFS is especially rare with severe conditions and a poor prognosis"]. One review covers recent diagnostic and treatment advances [6]. Another review is titled What Is Marfan Syndrome? [10] Diagnosis relies on the Ghent criteria [24: "The Ghent II Nosology of MFS criteria are crucial in MFS diagnosis"]. Related publications include PMID 2402263 [5]. Another is PMID 35894201 [9]. Another is PMID 37058316 [13]. Another is PMID 38517496 [17]. Another is PMID 8733052 [21].

## Aortic clinical trials

Trials targeting aortic root enlargement include Comparison of Two Medications Aimed at Slowing Aortic Root Enlargement in Individuals With Marfan Syndrome [8]. Another is Angiotensin Converting Enzyme Inhibitors in Marfan Syndrome [12]. Another is Losartan Versus Atenolol for the Treatment of Marfan Syndrome [16]. Another is A Randomized, Open-label, LOSARTAN Therapy on the Progression of Aortic Root Dilation in Patients With Marfan Syndrome [20]. A broader study is Studies of Heritable Disorders of Connective Tissue [4].
